title: Covariate sets that differ across comparators, and the ranking read from them
question: When one individual-data trial is compared with several aggregate comparators that report different covariates, does adjusting each contrast for everything it reports give a worse ranking than adjusting all contrasts for the common set, even though each contrast is less biased?
design: Unanchored MAIC of one trial against four comparators with nine covariates, 36 cells crossing reporting pattern, prognostic strength, similarity of comparator populations and separation of true effects, plus 8 control cells; maximal, intersection and bounded analyses. 1000 replicates per cell.
answer: Neither adjustment rule protects the ranking. The common (intersection) set ranked better in 15 of 36 scenarios and the maximal sets in 19; which wins depends on whether the omission bias pushes a lower-ranked comparator past a higher one, which the data do not show. The registered inversion was not confirmed in the primary scenarios, whose pattern turned out to widen the top comparator's lead, but held in all six Fawsitt-like scenarios with similar populations. The intersection's per-contrast bias was a median 2.4 times the maximal. A bounded analysis over the other comparators' reported means covered at least 0.93 with similar comparator populations at little extra width.
findings: Registered primary (strongest covariate missing for the top comparator, similar populations, tied effects): maximal sets lower on both bias and wrong-top-rank probability in 3 of 3 scenarios; verdict MAXIMAL VINDICATED.
Fawsitt-like pattern, similar populations: intersection lower wrong-top-rank probability in 6 of 6 scenarios, up to 0.94 against 0.31.
The difference between the two analyses did not predict a wrong top rank (AUROC 0.567).
Bounded interval coverage at least 0.929 with similar comparator populations at 1.00 to 1.99 times the maximal width; 0.678 at worst with dispersed populations. Maximal-set coverage fell to 0.086.
not_answered: Continuous outcome and independent covariates; non-collapsible outcomes, correlated omissions, a single ML-NMR network fit and overlap as a factor were not run. Three reporting patterns sample but do not exhaust where omissions can fall. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: B_k versus A mean difference in each comparator's population, and the ranking of the four
methods_compared: bounded interval over other comparators' reported means
